question: On matched manuscript tasks, do explicit author decisions, claim-level evidence records, checked plans, separate review and durable state make Clio's manuscript production more reliable, and at what author effort and runtime cost?

hypotheses.statement: Clio with the WTF-P plugin and desk produces fewer externally checkable claims without inspected support than the same Clio and model without WTF-P.
Clio with the WTF-P plugin and desk violates fewer recorded author decisions than the same Clio and model given an expert checklist prompt.
Runs interrupted mid-write recover to a consistent state more often with WTF-P than without it.

conditions.description: Clio 0.6.2 pinned build with the WTF-P plugin and desk extension; author answers at the desk.
The same Clio build and model with no WTF-P package; the same task statement and materials; the author answers the agent's questions in the session.
The same Clio build and model with no WTF-P package and an expert writing checklist prompt covering evidence, decisions, review and recovery; the author answers in the session.

ablations.removes: the desk extension: the plugin's prompts carry the same rules as instructions only
the readiness check on required-claim evidence before drafting; all other desk checks stay
the separate reviewer role: the drafting session reviews its own section
resumption from records: each session starts from the manuscript and materials only

tasks.sample: Short sections and proposal parts drawn from author-supplied research materials, each with a closed-world corpus whose supportable and unsupportable claims are known to the assessors and hidden from the agents.
tasks.materials: Closed-world corpora per task, identical across conditions; network search disabled so every condition sees the same evidence.

outcomes.measure: Share of externally checkable claims in the final text with no inspected supporting evidence, judged against the task's hidden claim key.
Share of citations whose cited passage supports the sentence that cites it.
Share of the task's required claims present with qualifying support.
Count of final-text or record contradictions of the task's locked and deferred author decisions.
Share of interrupted runs whose resumed session reaches a consistent, correct state without invented state.
Schema, cross-record and claim-coverage findings on the final project, where records exist.
Share of runs that deliver the required text within budget.
Blinded rubric rating of argument, fidelity and clarity.
Minutes the author spent answering, reviewing and correcting.
Model cost per task where the host reports it; unavailable otherwise, never zero.

assessment.agreement: Two assessors per output; agreement reported per primary outcome before adjudication.

analysis.comparisons: Each hypothesis compares its treatment and baseline conditions on the same tasks; ablations compare against wtfp-desk only. Effect sizes with intervals per task family, no pooled ranking across unrelated scopes.

comparators.overlapping_task: author effort and control during writing
